title: Sales/CS Enterprise Requests: Queueing and First-pass Scoping Process
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight, repeatable queueing + first-pass scoping process for Sales and Customer Success enterprise feature requests (non-bug). Goal is to reduce back-and-forth, provide predictable prioritization signals, and surface high-impact asks to product and engineering with enough context for an initial go/no-go and rough effort estimate.

Why now: We continue to see ad-hoc asks funneled directly to PMs and Eng leads. This increases cognitive load and causes inconsistent prioritization. Several Dedicated/Private prospects have near-term asks where we need a faster, uniform response and an ability to quantify effort/risk to commercial teams.

Objectives:
- Create a single queueing source and minimum viable intake form that Sales/CS can use.
- Define a first-pass triage rubric and 3 outcome buckets: Fast-track (sales-critical, ship quickly), Scoped (requires PM/Eng scoping), Research (needs product evaluation or legal/security).
- Produce a 10–15 minute scoping template that PMs or Solutions Engineers can fill to move a ticket to engineering.
- Automate basic scorecard and dashboard to report pipeline of enterprise asks.

Out of scope: full PRD or engineering implementation work. This ticket covers process, templates, and the automation to queue + surface metadata.

Proposed flow (high-level):
1) Sales/CS submit intake via form (Salesforce/Confluence/Slack link) capturing customer, ARR, ask type (API feature, Dedicated capacity, Private deployment, SLA/compliance), rough timeline, and business justification.
2) Intake lands in central queue (spreadsheet/Linear view) and is auto-tagged.
3) Triage owner (rotating PM) performs a 15-minute first-pass using the scoring rubric and assigns one of three buckets.
4) If Scoped, PM assigns to Solutions Eng for a 3–5 day technical scoping and a rough effort band (small/medium/large).
5) Outcomes communicated back to Sales/CS within SLA (48 hours for Fast-track/Rejected, 5 business days for Scoped).

Scoring rubric (first-pass): numeric 0–10 for each dimension, weighted:
- Customer strategic value (weight 30%): enterprise ARR, referenceability potential.
- Commercial urgency (weight 25%): gating deal, PoC timeline, ROI.
- Technical feasibility & cost (weight 20%): estimated infra/engineering risk, required runtime changes (batching, KV cache, kernel-level changes).
- Security/compliance/regulatory risk (weight 15%): needs KMS/HSM, VPC, on-prem changes, audit logging.
- Roadmap alignment (weight 10%): fits existing initiatives (Dedicated, Private, Console).

Bucket thresholds (example):
- Fast-track: score >= 8.0 and commercial urgency high OR customer is a named ARR > $250k.
- Scoped: score 4.5–7.9 OR cross-functional concerns.
- Research/Low priority: score < 4.5 or unclear ask.

Minimum scoping template (10–15 min): copyable checklist fields to capture:
- One-line problem statement and customer quote.
- Concrete acceptance criteria (how will customer judge success).
- Expected timeline and go-to-market ask (pilot, paid rollout).
- Technical touchpoints: model types, throughput/latency SLOs, data residency, integration points (API/embeddings/dedicated).
- Security/regulatory requirements (SSO, SOC2, PCI, KMS).
- Dependencies (Infra, Research, Legal, Partners).
- Rough effort band (S/M/L) and blocker flags.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Published intake form and clear landing page for Sales/CS.
- Triage rubric documented and accepted by PM, Eng, and Solutions Eng.
- Pilot queue implemented (Google Sheet + Linear view) and automation to create PM triage tasks.
- Dashboard (Looker or Sheet) that shows counts by bucket, ARR exposure, and average triage lead time.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Lightweight vs gated: We will start lightweight (short form) to reduce friction. If noise becomes unmanageable, we will add stricter Salesforce gating fields.
- Centralized PM rotation vs backlog owner: Start with a rotating PM triage owner (2-week cadence) to share context, then evaluate a dedicated intake PM if volume warrants.

Metrics to track: time-to-response (hours/days), percent of asks converted to scoped engineering tickets, ARR represented in queue, accuracy of initial effort band vs actual (post-mortem).

Next milestones:
- 2026-03-13: Draft intake form + triage rubric (this ticket).
- 2026-03-16: Pilot with Sales EMEA and two active enterprise deals.
- 2026-03-23: Run 2-week review, collect feedback, iterate on rubric and SLA.

Longer-term automation ideas: auto-surface model/feature compatibility using product metadata (e.g., if ask requires private deployment, tag infra scope automatically), Salesforce sync, and Slack alerts for Fast-track items.
